brief: Zero Hedge rounds up five skeptical takes on Anthropic's IPO on its first trading day. Anthropic priced at $83, above the range, raised over $107 billion, and traded up to 24% higher pre-open, helped by hedge funds sitting 11 points underweight tech. Seaport Research's Jay Goldberg models self-hosting open-weight rivals (DeepSeek V4 Pro, Kimi K3) against Anthropic's own prices. Self-hosting only beats Anthropic above roughly $2.4 million of annual spend, a threshold only Anthropic's largest customers clear, so the whales with the most dollars are exactly the ones who can defect. Anthropic has held off open-weight competition mainly by cutting token prices 50% in a month, which cost Q3 revenue about $600 million and pushed compute to 58% of sales, ending its first operating profit after one quarter. Bloomberg Intelligence prices the deal at 12-13x 2027 sales. Amundi's Mortier calls it excessive. Bloomberg Opinion's Kaissar argues most of the upside is already captured through Amazon and Alphabet's stakes and that LLM moats are shallow. Morgan Stanley's Hornbach flags an AI safety breach as the underpriced tail risk.
